completed.element: static <head>: structured data, social card, favicon
completed.summary: The static head made four false claims. Removed the fabricated aggregateRating (4.9 from 150 - LEGAL-002 removed the same fabrication from the runtime provider and missed this copy, the one crawlers read). Generated the 1200x630 og-image.png that og:image and twitter:image had pointed at since launch without either file existing. Repointed the Organization JSON-LD logo from the 404 /logo.png to /logos/logo.png and corrected its declared 512x512 to the real 2000x600. Dropped the SearchAction offering a sitelinks box at /search, which is not a route, and the msapplication-config pointing at a browserconfig.xml that does not exist. Separately, favicon.svg used React's stopColor instead of SVG's stop-color, so both gradients fell back to black - verified in Chromium, rgba(0,0,0,255) before, rgba(67,100,237,255) after. New guard: npm run check:seo-assets, CI-wired, zero-tolerance.

completed.element: the SEO surface now agrees with the coming-soon gate
completed.summary: Rendered the built app in Chromium and found the public site is behind App.tsx's COMING_SOON holding page (default ON - VITE_COMING_SOON must be 'false' to open it). The holding page sets noindex through usePageSeo, at RUNTIME, while the static head hardcoded index,follow - so every non-JS crawler was told to index 24 marketing URLs that all render the same page. A vite transformIndexHtml plugin now rewrites the robots meta from the same variable the gate reads, verified in both states. getSitemapRoutes takes the same flag: the sitemap dropped from 28 URLs to the 5 that actually render themselves while closed (signup, eula, privacy, terms, accessibility), which also corrects iteration 1 - it had published 24 URLs that serve a noindex page. COMING_SOON_ROUTES is asserted against App.tsx's Switch so the two cannot drift. robots.txt deliberately keeps no Disallow: / - a blocked crawler never sees the noindex.

completed.element: duplicate and unbacked tags in the head
completed.summary: Every page shipped two twitter:title, two twitter:description and two twitter:image tags: index.html wrote them as property= (not the Twitter Cards spec) while SEOProvider's setMeta defaults to name=, so its meta[name=...] query missed the static tag and appended a second one carrying the homepage's copy. Switched the static tags to name=, dropped twitter:url (the card reads og:url). SEOProvider also re-injected Organization and WebSite on every Organization-schema route, entities the static head already carries with stable @ids - removed, along with the runtime WebSite's SearchAction pointing at the same dead /search. Dropped article:modified_time, which was new Date() per render: a freshness claim produced by the act of viewing the page. Removed ORGANIZATION_DATA.contactPoint.telephone ('+1-800-PRINTYX' is not dialable and appears nowhere on the site) and LocalBusiness's priceRange '$$'; LocalBusiness now emits nothing without an address. Verified by render: 5 twitter tags in one set (was 10 in two), 5 distinct JSON-LD entities (was 7 with Organization and WebSite twice). check:seo-assets now compares the name-vs-property attribute between index.html and every SEOProvider setMeta call.

SEODashboard (2333 lines, routed at /seo) was written against a /api/seo/<noun>/<verb> URL scheme; server/routes-seo.ts registers /api/seo/<verb>/<noun>. Twelve of its endpoints POST to a path no router has, so they fail in dev AND production. The Express implementations are genuine - real Drizzle tables, PageSpeed Insights for Core Web Vitals, which throws without a key rather than inventing numbers - so the two halves were simply never connected. Repointed the four that differ by URL alone (mobile/analyze, performance/check, security/analyze, semantic/analyze): body keys and response shapes already matched. The other eight need body-key or response-shape work, or have no backend at all, and the whole set is missing from supabase/functions/seo, which serves production - all filed as SEO-004. Corrected the edge-coverage baseline note, which recorded these as prod-only gaps when they are dead in dev too. Edge-coverage ratchet 72 -> 68.
